- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; increase forecast by 3–7% for first 5 days if sentiment swings > 0.5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.7, -0.5, +0.7), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is > 10% above 30d forecast, model is biased low; apply upward bias of 5–8% for next 7 days if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias if price is above 30-day moving average.
